finding.text: `Dropped.js` walks the last 30 days of session folders and follows task refs itself (`day_dirs`/`collect`, Servex/Dropped.js:53-101), a second independent file-discovery traversal alongside `TaskLoop.find_task_files()`/`walk()` (Servex/TaskLoop.js:181-193) that does nearly the same thing (skip dotfiles/node_modules, follow module-task refs) over a different window. Two walkers to keep in sync is the kind of duplication the "one of everything" rule warns about; worth folding into one shared walker later, not a blocker now since it is tested and the windows genuinely differ (2 days vs 30).

`Servex/Dropped.js` is not listed in `Servex/readme.md`'s class diagram or "Where the code is" table, so a reader starting from the Servex module index alone would not learn it exists — though it is linked from `Servex/doc/task-loop.md`, `core/Task/readme.md` and `queue/readme.md`, and this matches the existing precedent of `Budget.js` (also undocumented there), so it's a minor gap, not a new one.

The brief says "a node check, run at every heartbeat" (requirements.md item 1); the build instead runs inside `TaskLoop.tick()` (Servex/TaskLoop.js:261-263), not `Heartbeat.js`. The session log's own summary names this correctly ("wired into TaskLoop.tick"), and functionally it still runs on a short fixed interval with no AI involved, so the owner's intent (a periodic, code-only check) is met even though the literal module named in the brief differs.

`Server/DoneCheck.mjs` is a new node script under `Server/` but isn't added to `Server/readme.md`'s "Scripts (one line each)" index (Server/readme.md:23-41) or `doc/script-notes.md`, breaking the "index everything you create" rule the rest of that list follows — a reader who opens the Server module index alone would never learn this script exists.

`public/framework/core/Task/doc/completion.md:861-863` ("Still to build: 5 ... 6 ...") is already one step behind the session's own log: `session.jsonl:14` (after this diff's last commit) reports item 5 needs no new code ("Prompt.completion and Question inherit Task.completion"). Not a blocker — a fresh agent who also reads `session.jsonl` gets the update — but the committed doc itself should catch up at the next edit so it doesn't silently drift further as item 6 proceeds.

Confirmed this is all on the unmerged `worktree/completion` branch (head `b480b8d28`, not yet in `michael/dev`); `node Servex/Dropped.test.mjs`, `node Server/DoneCheck.test.mjs` and `node public/framework/core/Task/Task.test.mjs` all pass (65/65) in that worktree. No code defects found in `Dropped.js`'s `judge()`/`rates()`/`collect()` or `DoneCheck.mjs`'s evidence check against the test cases and a manual read.

Requirement item 1 asks for a check "run at every heartbeat"; it runs inside `TaskLoop.tick()` instead (Servex/TaskLoop.js, `Dropped.tick()` call) — already caught and accepted by the prior fresh review (`review.jsonl` finding 3) as meeting the owner's intent (periodic, code-only) even though the named module differs.

Item 6 of requirements.md ("close this session properly," walk the 302 open tasks to 100% accounted for) is explicitly deferred in `completion.md`'s "Still to build" list and `session.jsonl`'s own next-steps line (merge, restart, run DoneCheck, walk the 253) — an honest, disclosed partial step rather than a silent gap, consistent with the owner's "keep working, never wait" rule.
